title: POC Weekly - Latency Tuning - Rivermark
summary: Weekly POC sync to review latency benchmarks (TTFT and tail latency), discuss streaming behavior, sequence length profiles, and kernel/quantization tradeoffs. Agreed to run two additional benchmark passes (streaming with small chunks + pre-warm KV cache) and validate on dedicated pool in staging. Action items assigned for benchmark spreadsheet updates and follow-up on Dedicated sizing and SSO/KMS questions.
topics: Dedicated vs hosted routing and pre-warming
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-18
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jonas (Redwood SE), Lina (Rivermark), Samir (Rivermark), Priya (Rivermark)

Summary/Notes (auto): go through latest benchmark CSV, discuss TTFT delta after changing to streaming=true and smaller chunk size, look at kernel flags for A100 vs T4 profiles, plan next benchmark runs.

[00:00] Maya: All right hi everyone thanks for joining, uh Lina Samir Priya, thanks for making time. we're on for the weekly POC sync, focus on latency tuning today, TTFT and streaming, Jonas will walk through the numbers.
[00:18] Lina: Hey thanks Maya, hey Jonas. quick note, we're trying to hit 200ms TTFT for our interactive chat use case, and 95th below 800ms if possible. those are our targets.
[00:32] Jonas: Got it, thanks. quick agenda: one, recap last week's run; two, streaming chunk size experiments; three, sequence length distribution and padding impact; four, kernel/quantization options; five, next steps.
[00:45] Samir: sounds good. also we had a question about dedicated pool pre-warm and whether Redwood can pin model to a warm cache, and how that affects cost.
[00:58] Jonas: yes we'll cover pre-warm options — warm KV cache and instance pinning — tradeoffs on cost.

[01:15] Jonas: ok so slide one — last week's baseline: hosted run on rwd-open-7b-quant (our internal name) on an A100 profile, batch size 1, streaming=false. median TTFT was ~340ms, p95 ~980ms, p99 ~1.6s. our logs show most of the time spent in kernel selection & attention matmul for 1k context when sequence length hits 512.
[01:45] Lina: that matches what we saw. we also noticed cold-starts added ~300ms for the first few requests in a node.
[01:55] Maya: to clarify cold starts — that's model load + kernel JIT or is it warm cache?
[02:05] Jonas: mostly kv-cache cold; also some cuda kernel warmup if it's the first inference on that VM. for hosted we do some lazy kernel compilation on first pattern which adds latency.

[02:25] Priya: are those kernel compiles per model version? we want deterministic behavior for our SLAs.
[02:33] Jonas: compile is per kernel-codepath and per hardware; once compiled it's reused, but if you switch quantization profile or change sequence length substantially we can see recompile. for deterministic low-latency we'd recommend dedicated with pre-warm.

[02:50] Maya: ok next, streaming experiments — Jonas?
[02:55] Jonas: yes, we ran three streaming setups: streaming=false (baseline), streaming=true with 256-token chunks, streaming=true with 64-token chunks. Results: 256 chunks reduced median latency marginally to 320ms; 64-token chunking got us to 260ms median TTFT for short prompts (~40 tokens) but increased token throughput cost slightly due to more RPC edge calls. p95 improved to ~700ms for 64 chunking. p99 still spikes mostly on long sequences.
[03:30] Samir: interesting — so smaller chunks reduce TTFT but increase overhead. is that overhead mostly on the client side or server side?
[03:39] Jonas: mostly server-side scheduling and RPC overhead, plus a bit of edge latency with more SSE or websocket messages. we measured ~5-12ms extra per chunk. but importantly first token generation was faster because we can stream once partial attention warms.

[03:58] Lina: does Redwood support adaptive chunking? like start small for TTFT, then increase chunk size?
[04:05] Jonas: not out-of-the-box adaptive chunking yet; you can implement client-side heuristics to request small initial max_tokens and then larger follow-ups. we have an internal feature flag for adaptive streaming, roadmap item.

[04:22] Priya: ok on sequence length — we pushed a representative distribution. average user prompt+history is 78 tokens, but tails go up to 1,200 tokens for a small cohort (support transcripts). what's the best way to tune for that distribution?
[04:36] Jonas: two levers: dynamic batching + prefix KV caching. For prefix-heavy traffic, enabling KV cache persistence between requests (session pinning) reduces repeated compute. Also trimming the passed context or summarizing history reduces effective sequence length. We showed a trimmed-run where we truncated to last 200 tokens and saw p95 drop from 980ms to ~620ms.

[04:58] Samir: how disruptive is session pinning to multi-tenant capacity? if we pin a session per user for days, do we run out of KV memory?
[05:06] Jonas: correct — pinned KV caches consume GPU memory. For Hosted, we have TTL and LRU eviction; for Dedicated you can configure longer TTLs but you'll need to size the pool accordingly. we can estimate required memory based on active sessions. we'll add that to the sizing doc.

[05:26] Maya: let's talk kernel choices and quantization next. Jonas, what did we test?
[05:30] Jonas: we tested int8 quant (awq) vs int4 (gptq-ish) vs bfloat16. Observations: int8 gave ~1.15x speed-up, with small quality delta; int4 gained ~1.6x speed-up but increased p99 hallucination rate slightly on the eval set. Kernel tuning: using fused attention kernels for A100 improved throughput; on T4 some kernels are slower so we fallback to generic cuda kernels which increases latency variance.
[06:02] Lina: we plan to run on a mix of A100 and smaller GPU pools in prod. is Redwood able to route based on model variant vs hardware cost?
[06:10] Jonas: yes — smart routing can route low-priority traffic to cost-optimized pooled nodes; you can pin critical requests to A100-backed Dedicated capacity. We can also set fallback policies when capacity is saturated.

[06:25] Priya: about quantization — are you seeing any issues with tool calls or structured outputs when using lower precision?
[06:32] Jonas: occasionally tokenization boundaries can produce slight diffs, mostly minor. For strict correctness we recommend int8 or bfloat16; int4 is best for cost-sensitive pipelines with a human-in-the-loop QA.

[06:48] Samir: any quick wins we can do this week to move TTFT from 340 to sub-250 for our main flow?
[06:53] Jonas: yes a few: enable streaming with 64-token initial chunks, turn on prefix KV cache for authenticated sessions, switch to A100 kernels (if you can route to A100), and enable light quant (int8). Combined we estimate median TTFT ~200-240ms. We'll run an integrated pass.

[07:10] Lina: cost impact? we need to present cost delta to ops.
[07:14] Maya: Jonas, can you quantify cost per 1M tokens for the int8 + A100+streaming config vs baseline?
[07:20] Jonas: rough numbers: baseline hosted (bf16-like) ~= $X per 1M tokens; with int8 + A100 + streaming we see ~20-30% lower per-token cost because of better batching and lower repeat compute, but dedicated pool hourly is higher so depends on utilization. we'll push a spreadsheet with estimates — see action items.

[07:38] Priya: about Dedicated pre-warm — will Redwood dedicate an entire GPU to our instances to avoid cold kernels?
[07:45] Jonas: yes, Dedicated lets you reserve capacity; you can pre-warm KV caches and keep instances pinned. There's an autoscaling policy to keep a minimum number of warm replicas. The tradeoff is cost for reserved capacity.

[07:58] Samir: our security team also asked about KMS and audit logs for Private deployment; any blockers for us?
[08:05] Maya: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and audit logs; we also have SOC2 docs and SAML SSO support. we'll attach the security pack.

[08:18] Lina: great — do you have an estimated timeline for a Dedicated staging run? we want to compare hosted vs dedicated in staging under our real workload.
[08:26] Maya: we can spin a small Dedicated pool in staging by next week if you sign the staging addendum; otherwise we can run extended hosted runs with pinned instances for a few hours.

[08:40] Jonas: for this week we propose three benchmark passes: 1) streaming=true, chunk=64, int8 on A100 profile; 2) streaming=true, chunk=256, int8 on mixed GPU profile; 3) dedicated small pool with KV pre-warm and session pinning for 2 hours. We'll run each for a 30-minute steady-state and collect p50/p95/p99 and cost.

[09:05] Samir: ok schedule that. also please include tail distribution for sequences >512 tokens.

[09:12] Lina: one ask — can you add a run with adaptive batching disabled to see worst-case single-request latency?
[09:18] Jonas: yes we can disable dynamic batching to measure single-request SLOs.

[09:26] Maya: quick crosstalk — 
[09:30] (background) Priya: sorry one sec — I've got a quick infra note: our staging VPC restricts egress so we might need IP allowlist for hosted endpoints, how does Redwood handle that?
[09:42] Jonas: we have egress-friendly options: Private connects and VPC peering for Redwood Private, and we can provide static egress IPs for Dedicated. we'll document specifics in the network runbook.

[09:58] Lina: any issues with streaming on mobile clients? we saw jitter once in a while.
[10:05] Jonas: streaming over lossy mobile links can cause out-of-order events; we recommend an ack mechanism or slight client buffering. small chunk sizes worsen jitter frequency but improve TTFT. it's a tradeoff.

[10:24] Maya: ok let's go through action items and next steps. Jonas can you recap the benchmark plan and owners?
[10:30] Jonas: sure — benchmarks: (A) 64-chunk streaming + int8 on A100 — owner: Jonas; (B) 256-chunk streaming + int8 mixed GPUs — owner: Jonas; (C) Dedicated small pool pre-warm with session pinning — owner: Maya to coordinate provisioning, Jonas run tests; (D) adaptive-batching disabled run — owner: Samir to validate configuration we supply. each run we'll collect CSV profiles and token-level traces.

[10:58] Samir: timeline?
[11:00] Jonas: we'll start runs tomorrow and aim to have results by Friday EOD.

[11:06] Priya: we'll also need the security pack for the SRE review — can you send SOC2 + KMS docs?
[11:12] Maya: yes, I'll share the security pack and the sizing spreadsheet after this call.

[11:20] Lina: excellent. one more question — you mentioned kernel compilation can re-trigger if sequence patterns change; how do we avoid that in prod?
[11:28] Jonas: avoid frequent switching of quant profiles or model variants; stabilize the runtime flags, and use Dedicated pinned nodes for high-SLA traffic. also we can pre-generate kernels for expected pattern distributions as part of onboarding.

[11:44] Maya: ok wrapping up — recap quick: run three benchmarks, share CSV & cost spreadsheet, schedule Dedicated staging if Rivermark approves staging addendum, send security pack. next call same time next week, we'll review results.

[11:58] (short crosstalk) 
[12:05] Lina: thanks everyone.
[12:08] Maya: thanks, bye.
